target_customer: Brazilian micro and small business owners and self-employed workers who need weekly working capital credit
problem: Self-employed and micro business owners in Brazil have little access to affordable short term credit; Zippi lets them pay suppliers by Pix and settle weekly.
business_model: Lending with a service fee (3 to 4 percent) on the credit used, funded by credit funds (FIDC)
product_category: Fintech, working capital credit for micro and small businesses

founders.name: Andre Bernardes
prior_employers: Bank of America Merrill Lynch (over five years structuring products)

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit underwriting, collections and Pix integration; needed in house risk models but standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Underwriting data on small business behavior and funding relationships help, but banks and fintechs target the same segment.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Digital banks and fintechs entered the small business segment over time; Zippi still raised a Series A in 2022 and debt funds in 2025.

market_need_then: Brazil has over 24 million self-employed workers (IBGE, as cited by press) and 22 million small businesses with little credit access.

identity.logo: A megaphone meant to give voice to the self-employed (Finsiders Brasil, 2022)
identity.visual_style: A Behance case study describes a brand designed to look distinct from other financial brands

branding.brand_signature: Megaphone logo giving voice to the self-employed

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive short name and a clear symbol with a purpose story, but no evidence of community or viral reach.

pivots.from: Personal loan platform for the self-employed
pivots.to: Savings style account, then accounts payable and receivable tools
Weekly working capital credit card, then Pix based weekly credit in 2021
pivots.why: Settled on weekly credit; customers adopted Pix.

outcome_analysis: Zippi was formed at MIT around 2019, tried three products, and found traction with weekly working capital credit, later built on Pix. It raised $450K from YC and Canary in 2019, a $5M seed in 2021 and a $16M Series A led by Tiger Global in 2022-06, then credit funds from Itau, Bradesco Asset and Verde in 2025. It reports R$1 billion credit volume and about 100,000 clients and is active with about 60 people.
notes: Education of ITA for two founders comes from search summaries of Brazilian press and was not opened; MIT MBA is from Finsiders Brasil. The 2019 $450K check is not labeled by the article. The FIDC debt of R$85M (2025-09) and a later R$220M FIDC with Credit Saison are in BRL and not converted; the R$220M is not recorded because only a search snippet was seen. Competitors: the 2022 Finsiders article names FinMatch, Bom, Baduk, Neon, BizCapital, Cora, Linker, Justa, Listo and banks as competitors, but it is dated 2022, so it is not used for competition as of 2019 and the list is empty. Founding year: one summary says the founders returned to Brazil in 2018.
